People who have eaten a strange animal what was it and how was the taste?

I have eaten an Australian possum and it tastes almost exactly the same as pork. Salt water crocodile tastes like fish but the flesh is much firmer. Kangaroo is very lean meat and has a taste that is a bit gamey but has it's own unique taste that's kinda hard to compare to other meats.

There's a restaurant around here called 'Game' that's serves a lot of exotic shit, but I never get around to it.

Crocodile is yum, especially in wontons. Jellyfish salad, however, is the most repulsive thing I have ever tasted.

I have had lion. Very "feline" tasting. It made my kitchen smell like wet cat. The store sold me meat patties but mentioned three or four times that it could be used to make chilli. I ended up making chilli.

I ate on those scorpion lollipops you can get at a truck stop in the southwestern U.S. The lollipop part was pretty good, above average. But the scorpion was vile. I've heard stories of people using small, non-breakthrough doses of LSD as a sort of mood and creativity enhancer. Yesterday, I ingested approximately fifty micros of LSD -- which, according to Erowid, is considered both a "light" and "common" quantity -- opened up WordPad, and wrote down the following musings throughout the day.

TL;DR:

1:35pm
I drove to the park, sat in my car and listened to music, watching people walk on the trail, watching the trees, and the birds, and a long-legged spider make its way across my windshield. It was, overall, a pleasant, revitalizing experience-- and now I know what people mean when they say they took acid once, but fail to mention the intense visuals or loss of reality. I was able to remain coherent at this dosage. However, I could still experience the pleasant auras, both inwardly and in nature, that come with such a trip.

NOTES:
along with the time, if I remembered to write it down.

6:48am
Ingested 50ug orally.

7:24am
Tab was a little thicker than I'm used to, so I ended up swallowing it as holding it under my tongue became awkward. Watching Interstellar.

7:37am
Noticing some slight changes in visual perception, it's also getting slightly more difficult to type. Having unusual -- but not necessarily unpleasant -- changes in thought patterns. My body is at times feeling flushed, and other times shivering. I've prepared for this in advance, and have a warm hoodie, a snuggie, and a t-shirt to alternate between. I also have a Benadryl and Klonopin to put myself to sleep, and quell anxiety, should the need arise.

7:52am
I'm smiling and cracking up at the most senseless things, especially online, and in scenes from Interstellar. Visual effects are hard to describe, but not in the regular "kaleidoscopic LSD experience with fractals everywhere" sort of way... it's almost a surreal, dreamscape that I've found myself in. Like I'm somewhat detached from the real world in the most wonderful way, but can still completely comprehend it.

8:06am
I'm definitely feeling more like an "infant", thinking how it's likely a good thing new memories aren't formed until later in life, otherwise our earliest memories would be really wonky.

Currently wearing both hoodie and snuggie. Feeling love and bemusement and comfort in everything.

I'm starting to think I understand it, but it's becoming increasingly difficult to articulate: the total brain connectivity and connectedness with the universe trippers often describe is simply us, as rational adults, attempting to rationalize a pre-language experience, one we all had as infants, without a language. We're truly re-experiencing what it was like in our earliest childhoods. A time before we learned language.

As I'm writing this I can see the green, yellow, and purple fragments of each letter I type -- with a ghost of cyan -- clinging to each letter, almost insignificantly. I think I know what's causing this effect but my mind is wandering too much to put it into words. It has to do with LCD displays.

8:30am
I still have work that needs to be done; clients and responsibilities and such. It's going to be challenging in this mindframe but I'll certainly try to do my best.

8:48am
Stared into the mirror for an indefinite amount of time. Had a real LSD breakthrough, the first of which I assume are more to come. Watched my face morph and turn into a peacock-like array of colors and patterns.

The normally unnoticeable soap spots on the mirror connected with one another, as if geometrically, which added to the patterns on my face, in their own geometric way.

It's getting hard to keep a single train of though. I won't be able to write like this much longer. Things are moving and shifting too much, it's unusually difficult to focus. Normal LSD experience, but I wasn't expecting this number of visuals, along with this degree of introspectiveness.

I'm watching fractals appear on my computer screen, making it hard to work and type. Usually they stay in the background, behind the scenes, but occasionally an entire word or letter or paragraph turns into a colorful tunnel, which breathes and blends with the tunnels around it, the geometric endlessness.

I can definitely see how LSD might someday be used as an antidepressant
